videos.title: 28.09.26 - RIFT Education Day
videos.summary_source_text:
28.09.26 - RIFT Education Day RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

RIFT — THE NEXT-GEN AFFILIATE OS

Learn. Participate. Manage Risk. Think Bigger. RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

videos.summary_source_text:
Hindi - 28.09.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

videos.summary_source_text:
Blue Jackets GM Don Waddell Breaks Down BLOCKBUSTER Marchenko-Knies Trade ft. Greg Wyshynski A blockbuster trade rocks the NHL on the eve of the 2026-27 season, and Columbus Blue Jackets GM Don Waddell joins Jeff Marek and Greg Wyshynski to break it all down. Hours after Columbus sent Kirill Marchenko, Elvis Merzlikins and Miles Wood to the Toronto Maple Leafs for Matthew Knies, Steven Lorentz, Emil Andrae and a 2027 second-round pick, Waddell explains why the Blue Jackets made the move, the decision to move on from Marchenko, what Columbus believes it is getting in Knies and how the trade came together. Waddell also discusses Adam Fantilli’s new six-year, $82.5 million contract, the importance of getting one of the franchise’s cornerstone players locked up long term and where the Blue Jackets stand following a headline-filled summer. Then, with the NHL regular season getting underway, Jeff and Greg go around the league with the biggest opening-night stories, predictions, bold takes and everything to watch as the 2026-27 season begins.

videos.title: The Most Critical Move for Deceptive Hockey Players
videos.summary_source_text:
The Most Critical Move for Deceptive Hockey Players The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

videos.title: Best Kirill Marchenko and Matthew Knies Career Plays
videos.summary_source_text:
Best Kirill Marchenko and Matthew Knies Career Plays 26-year-old forward Kirill Marchenko was traded to the Toronto Maple Leafs from the Columbus Blue Jackets as part of a six-player deal that saw Matthew Knies go back to Columbus.

Marchenko, who could have become a restricted free agent after this season, signed a six-year, $75 million contract ($12.5 million average annual value) with the Maple Leafs that starts next season, according to his agent.

In addition to Marchenko, the Maple Leafs also acquired forward Miles Wood and goalie Elvis Merzlikins. Going to Columbus with Knies was forward Steven Lorentz and defenseman Emil Andrae and a second-round pick in the 2027 NHL Draft.

videos.title: PEANUT BUTTER DOES WHAT?! Eat This and Watch What Happens | Dr. Mandell
videos.summary_source_text:
PEANUT BUTTER DOES WHAT?! Eat This and Watch What Happens | Dr. Mandell Peanut butter has been misunderstood for years. Because it’s rich, calorie-dense, and contains fat, many people automatically assume it’s a food they should avoid—especially when they’re trying to manage their weight or improve their metabolic health. But what matters isn’t simply whether a food contains fat; it’s the overall nutritional package and how it fits into your diet. Natural peanut butter provides predominantly unsaturated fats along with plant protein, fiber, magnesium, vitamin E, niacin, and other beneficial nutrients and plant compounds. That combination of fat, protein, and fiber can help slow digestion, increase fullness, and make a meal or snack more satisfying, which may help reduce the urge to keep reaching for highly refined foods between meals. Peanut butter can also change the way carbohydrates affect you when the foods are eaten together because adding fat, protein, and fiber to a carbohydrate-containing meal can slow digestion and moderate the rise in blood glucose compared with eating the carbohydrate by itself. Peanuts and other nuts have also been extensively studied as part of dietary patterns associated with cardiovascular and metabolic health, and replacing foods high in saturated fat with foods containing more unsaturated fats can help support healthier cholesterol levels. Peanut butter also provides fiber that contributes to digestive health and regularity, while its nutrient density makes a relatively small serving surprisingly satisfying. The important part is choosing a peanut butter that is primarily peanuts—ideally without large amounts of added sugar or hydrogenated fats—and remembering that portion size still matters because peanut butter is calorie-dense. Try a spoonful with an apple, celery, oatmeal, or a smoothie, or simply enjoy it by itself. And these principles aren’t limited to peanut butter; almond butter and other minimally processed nut butters can provide many of the same nutritional advantages. Healthy eating isn’t about fearing fat or labeling one food as magical—it’s about choosing nutrient-dense foods that help you stay satisfied and make your overall diet easier to maintain. If you’ve been avoiding peanut butter because you thought it was automatically “fattening,” this video may completely change the way you look at that spoonful.

videos.summary_source_text:
NHL Cracks Down on Jerseys, Salary Cap Surge, and Sabres Questions ft. David Pagnotta & Mike Augello The latest NHL news and biggest hockey storylines are front and centre on The Sheet with Jeff Marek. Jeff is joined by NHL insider David Pagnotta to break down the league’s latest uniform and equipment enforcement, including players being penalized for wearing their jerseys tucked in, what could be next when it comes to NHL player visors, and the potential impact of the NHL salary cap continuing to rise over the next two seasons. Jeff and Dave also have a special announcement you won’t want to miss. Later, Mike Augello of Hockey Hotstove joins Jeff to take a deep dive into the Buffalo Sabres after their breakthrough 2025-26 season. They discuss Buffalo’s summer, the Sabres’ roster changes, the ongoing questions surrounding Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen and Alex Lyon, the team’s goaltending situation heading into the new season, expectations for the Sabres after their return to the Stanley Cup Playoffs, and what comes next for a young Buffalo team looking to build on its success. Plus, more NHL news, analysis, rumours and insider information from around the league on The Sheet with Jeff Marek.

videos.title: OpenAI’s “Always-On Assistant” Changes CHATGPT Forever
videos.summary_source_text:
OpenAI’s “Always-On Assistant” Changes CHATGPT Forever https://bitbiased.ai/ai-automation-services

A leaked ChatGPT upgrade screen suggests OpenAI could be preparing a $100 tier featuring "o, your always-on assistant." Meanwhile, Microsoft has officially introduced Copilot Autopilot, Google has launched Gemini 3.8 Live Avatar, and OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol is reportedly reaching 750 tokens per second on Cerebras hardware.

Are AI assistants finally becoming autonomous workers that keep working after you close the app? Or is "always-on AI" being misunderstood?

The answer is more complicated than the headlines suggest.

On September 26, a Reddit user shared what appeared to be an unreleased ChatGPT Pro upgrade screen. The alleged "Frontier Intelligence – Standard" tier listed more Work and Codex usage, maximum memory, 100 GB of file storage, and a mysterious assistant called "o."

But the screenshot hasn't been independently corroborated. OpenAI hasn't confirmed the plan, the $100 billing period, or what "o" actually does. Even the reported configuration details, including an email suffix associated with the assistant, don't establish that it can independently read messages or take action.

And that's where the comparison with Microsoft and Google gets interesting.

Microsoft's Copilot Autopilot, formerly Scout, is a documented example of a persistent AI agent. It can have its own Entra identity, memory, workspace, and objectives. Microsoft's examples show agents coordinating supplier reviews, preparing documents, monitoring responses, following up with stakeholders, and requesting human approval for certain actions.

Unlike the OpenAI leak, Copilot Autopilot is an officially announced product, although it remains in private preview with usage-based billing.

Google's Gemini 3.8 Live Avatar approaches the problem differently. Announced September 24, it combines real-time lip-synced video, multilingual speech across 97 languages, custom enterprise avatars, and asynchronous tool execution.

That last capability is particularly interesting: Google's avatar can continue speaking while a background tool handles something like a hotel booking. But it doesn't mean the avatar continues pursuing objectives after the conversation ends.

These systems reveal an important distinction between persistent AI agents, proactive automation, and conversational interfaces that feel more autonomous.

We also examine the infrastructure making this possible.

OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol Ultrafast mode reportedly delivers approximately 750 output tokens per second using Cerebras WSE-3 hardware, around 14 times standard API throughput. But throughput isn't the same as first-token latency, and there's no confirmed connection between Cerebras acceleration and the leaked assistant "o."

Then there's the catch: cost and security.

A traditional chatbot answers individual requests. A persistent agent may repeatedly inspect messages, retrieve context, execute tools, update memory, and interact with external services. Those operations introduce ongoing inference costs, storage requirements, and potentially substantial usage-based bills.

And granting an AI assistant continuous access to email, calendars, files, and business applications creates serious security questions.

We examine OAuth permissions, administrative controls, audit trails, memory poisoning, and EchoLeak (CVE-2025-32711), a Microsoft Copilot vulnerability that demonstrated how malicious content could manipulate an AI assistant into exposing sensitive information.

An agent having its own identity doesn't automatically make it autonomous. And an assistant described as "always-on" doesn't necessarily mean a language model is continuously running.

The bigger question is what happens when AI systems can maintain objectives, respond to events, and act with delegated permissions while users are away.

With OpenAI DevDay scheduled for September 29, attention is turning toward whether the company will reveal more about "o." No announcement is confirmed, and several essential questions remain unanswered.

What triggers the assistant? What applications can it access? How much autonomy does it actually have? What does $100 buy? And can users inspect, approve, reverse, or stop its actions?

We break down the evidence, compare the actual products, separate documented capabilities from speculation, and explore what this shift could mean for the future of AI agents.

CHAPTERS

01:38 The Screenshot, and Everything It Actually Proves
03:44 What "Always-On" Really Means
04:55 Microsoft Autopilot Is the Closest Thing to the Real Product
06:17 Google's Avatar Is a Different Animal
07:17 Identity Is Not Autonomy
08:09 Why This Is Possible Right Now
09:29 The Bill Nobody Puts on the Slide
10:32 Permissions Are the Real Bottleneck
11:36 Where This Lands, and What to Watch

Business Before the Business | 32 Thoughts In this edition of 32 Thoughts, Kyle Bukauskas and Elliotte Friedman begin the podcast by discussing the unfinished business that is sprinkled around the NHL and still has to be resolved as we enter the regular season. They talk about the cap estimate at $127.5m. The fellas update the Alexander Nikishin situation with Carolina. Elliotte talks about the Oilers looking for a right-shot centre. The guys talk about Nikita Kucherov entering the final year of his deal without an extension. They also talk about a few goalies of interest that popped up on the waivers on Sunday. The fellas have a laugh at the Flyers doing warm-ups with their jerseys tucked in in solidarity with Trevor Zegras. Elliotte compliments the Hurricanes on their Cup rings. videos.summary_source_text:
Small Knee Bends, Quick Steps, Just Enough To Make Them Bite The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

videos.summary_source_text:
I Tested TWO of Golf's FASTEST Drivers…Here's What I Found Looking for the best golf driver of 2026? In this Callaway Quantum vs Titleist GTS3 driver comparison, Mark Crossfield puts two of the fastest new golf drivers head-to-head to discover how they compare and which one could be right for your golf game.

The new Callaway Quantum Triple Diamond Max and Titleist GTS3 driver promise impressive ball speeds, distance and performance. But which driver delivers the best combination of speed, forgiveness, consistency and control?

In this driver comparison video, Mark conducts a full Callaway Quantum Triple Diamond Max driver review and Titleist GTS3 driver review, comparing their technology, appearance, sound, feel and adjustability before putting both drivers through extensive testing.

Discover how the Callaway's AI-optimised face, adjustable perimeter weighting and carbon construction compare with the Titleist's Speed Synced Face, SureFit CG weighting system and aerodynamic design.

Using launch monitor data, Mark compares driver ball speed, carry distance, launch conditions and spin rates to establish whether either driver delivers a meaningful performance advantage. He also explores how each driver's weighting system and natural shot shape could influence your performance.

But launch monitor numbers only tell part of the story. Mark takes both drivers onto the golf course to see how their performance translates into real playing conditions, testing their consistency, shot-shaping capabilities, sound and feel.

With both drivers producing exceptional ball speeds and remarkably similar distances, choosing between the Callaway Quantum Triple Diamond Max and Titleist GTS3 might come down to more than simply hitting the longest drives.

Mark also compares the Callaway Quantum prices with the Titleist GTS 3 prices, and explains which driver he would personally choose, considering everything from performance and adjustability to appearance, sound and feel.

If you're considering buying a new golf driver in 2026, wondering whether the Callaway Quantum or Titleist GTS3 is worth your money, or simply want to see how two of golf's biggest manufacturers compare, this comprehensive driver test should help you understand what each model has to offer.

I gave my Claude AI trading bot $100 and one challenge: double the account in 22 hours.

Could an AI trading bot discover its own strategies, test them and trade real money successfully?

Instead of asking Claude to predict the entire market, I gave it one specific task: predict whether the next 15-minute candle would finish higher or lower.

But there was a problem. Winning trades paid less than losing trades cost. Once fees were included, a 50% win rate would lose money.

So before risking the $100, I gave Claude two hours to research and backtest strategies using TradingKit. It tested over 1,600 strategies across more than 34,000 variants, narrowed them down through validation and selected five for live trading.

Then we hit another obstacle: the broker’s up-or-down product had no API available for this setup. Claude built a Chrome extension to automate the trades through my browser.

You’ll see the complete setup, the prompts, the strategy dashboard, the first painful loss, the final trade and the account’s results. Did the AI trading bot actually double my money, or was this another experiment that looked better in a backtest?

Could an AI trading bot discover its own strategies, test them and trade real money successfully?

But there was a problem. Winning trades paid less than losing trades cost. Once fees were included, a 50% win rate would lose money.

So before risking the $100, I gave Claude two hours to research and backtest strategies using TradingKit. It tested over 1,600 strategies across more than 34,000 variants, narrowed them down through validation and selected five for live trading.

Signs of Nutritional Deficiency (Pale Skin, Thinning Hair, Bleeding Gums, Dandruff) These common signs can point to specific nutritional deficiencies. Your skin, nails, hair, gums, and even certain cravings can give you clues about the nutrients you’re missing.

🌟 Take the 2-minute Health Lever Quiz: https://drbrg.co/4ruU5V6

Just so you know, my full line of high-quality supplements is available on Amazon — search Dr. Berg Supplements. 

Common signs of nutritional deficiencies include:
• Pale skin — Vitamin B12
• Cracking at the corners of the mouth — Vitamin B2
• Ridges on the fingernails — Iron
• White spots on the nails — Zinc
• Bleeding gums — Vitamin C
• Thinning outer eyebrows — Iodine
• Restless legs at night — Magnesium
• Calf cramps — Magnesium
• Thinning hair — Biotin
• Cold hands and feet — Vitamin B12
• Dark circles under the eyes — Iron or Vitamin K
• Craving ice — Iron
• Dandruff — Omega-3 fatty acids

Get to 90 degrees of hinge by left arm parallel, trail wrist bent back 75 percent, and fully released at 45 degrees past impact — and watch how the Adam Scott golf swing demonstrates every one of these checkpoints in a single motion. Matt Fitzpatrick’s Final 9 Holes in France | Every Shot Watch the Back 9 on Sunday, presented by Nexo, as Matt Fitzpatrick secured a three-shot victory at the 2026 FedEx Open de France to claim his 11th DP World Tour win and first FedEx Open de France title. 

► SUBSCRIBE: http://et.golf/Subscribe 

Michael Kim returns as defending champion to play in Europe for the first time since July, but this time he’ll be playing at a completely different course. He is joined by a field headlined by Ryder Cup stars such as Tommy Fleetwood, Matt Fitzpatrick, Ludvig Åberg, and Viktor Hovland who all arrive after competing at the BMW PGA Championship. They are joined by PGA Tour winners Kristoffer Reitan, Ryan Gerard and Cameron Smith. A strong home contingent featuring Matthieu Pavon and Adrien Saddier rounds off a phenomenal line-up. videos.title: Has George Cracked The Code? | Azerbaijan GP Review | F1 Nation Podcast
videos.summary_source_text:
Has George Cracked The Code? | Azerbaijan GP Review | F1 Nation Podcast Tom Clarkson, James Hinchcliffe and Alex Brundle sit down in the Baku paddock to dissect a thrilling Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

George Russell may have only won the race by a tenth after a dramatic drag race with Max Verstappen to the finish line, but he was dominant all weekend to take his third victory of the season.

Why was George back to his best in Baku? Has he finally got to grips with the car? And what does this result mean for his title challenge?

Kimi Antonelli recovered from his crash in qualifying to climb from P16 to P5. Given the Mercedes’ straight-line speed, why wasn’t he able to cut through the field as successfully as he did in Monza? And was this the first time we’ve seen Kimi race with the championship in mind?

The guys also discuss Red Bull's first double podium since China 2024 - whether Max could have won had he qualified higher up, the team orders between him and Isack Hadjar, and just how impressive the latter’s performance was after missing the previous three races with a wrist injury.

Elsewhere, there was mayhem in the midfield as Franco Colapinto took out Alpine teammate Pierre Gasly and McLaren’s Lando Norris at the first Safety Car restart, when Arvid Lindblad also hit his Racing Bulls teammate Liam Lawson. So what will the debriefs at Alpine and Racing Bulls look like?

Also on the agenda: Esteban Ocon’s future after leading Haas to a double points finish, a much-needed point for Williams, disappointment for Oscar Piastri having been in podium contention and an anonymous race for Ferrari.

Who’s ready for an American vs Japan showdown?! 

We’ve got our hands on a 4th generation Dodge Viper ACR, and it’s lining up against the legendary Lexus LFA! 

The question is, which V10 will make it to the finish line first? Let’s take a closer look at the stats…

First up we have the Dodge Viper ACR. It’s powered by an 8.4-litre naturally aspirated V10 which produces 608hp and 760Nm. However, it’s had a slight tune applied to it, meaning the output is more likely to be around 650hp and 800Nm! videos.summary_source_text:
Jon Machota: Cowboys Had the Game Won — Then Blew It The Cowboys had a chance to win in Brazil — and Clarence Hill and The Athletic's Jon Machota aren't letting them off the hook.

After Dallas' 34–31 loss to the Ravens, Clarence and Jon break down a brutal finish that saw the Cowboys fail to capitalize late. They discuss the final drive, Dak Prescott's decision-making, the Cowboys' offensive stars, the defense's final stand and the coaching decisions that helped turn a potential victory into an overtime loss.

They also look ahead to a brutal short week against the Houston Texans and the Cowboys' 1–2 start.

Plus: Why this loss felt particularly frustrating, and why Jon says this was as angry and frustrated as he's seen Dak Prescott after a regular-season game.

Cowboys 31, Ravens 34. Dallas heads to Houston.

The Presidents Cup heads to the iconic Medinah Country Club for its 16th edition, with the International Team looking to end the U.S. dominance on home soil. Scottie Scheffler headlines the American side alongside Cameron Young, Wyndham Clark, Sam Burns, Xander Schauffele and Justin Thomas, while the Internationals are led by Adam Scott, making his record-equalling 12th Presidents Cup appearance, alongside Hideki Matsuyama, Si Woo Kim and Open Champion Ryan Fox. Medinah’s newly transformed Course No. 3 provides a fresh test at 7,548 yards, with Geoff Ogilvy returning as International captain after helping oversee the redesign. The U.S. are seeking an 11th consecutive Presidents Cup victory, while the Internationals aim to claim their first win since 1998. The Main Difference Between Hockey and Basketball The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

videos.title: Numbness, Tingling & Burning? These 7 Nutrients Can Help Your Nerves | Dr. Mandell
videos.summary_source_text:
Numbness, Tingling & Burning? These 7 Nutrients Can Help Your Nerves | Dr. Mandell If you’re experiencing numbness, tingling, burning, stabbing sensations, or other symptoms associated with irritated or damaged nerves, there are important nutrients that play roles in normal nerve and nervous-system function. In this video, Dr. Alan Mandell explains several nutritional compounds associated with nerve health, inflammation, metabolic health, and healthy nerve signaling. Neuropathy can have many different causes, including diabetes, nutritional deficiencies, medication effects, alcohol use, injury, and certain medical conditions, so understanding and addressing the underlying cause is extremely important. Supporting your body with proper nutrition may be an important part of maintaining healthy nerves and normal nerve function. Persistent, unexplained, or worsening numbness, weakness, burning, or pain should always be properly evaluated. 

THE 7 NERVE-SUPPORTING NUTRIENTS & COMPOUNDS DISCUSSED:

Turmeric / Curcumin — Antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties; black pepper (piperine) can substantially increase curcumin absorption.
B Vitamins (B1, B6 & B12) — Important for normal nerve and nervous-system function. B12 deficiency can cause neurological symptoms; excessive supplemental B6 can also damage nerves.
Omega-3 Fatty Acids — EPA and DHA provide important structural fats used by cells throughout the body, including the nervous system.
Vitamin D — Important for normal immune, muscle, bone, and nervous-system function.
Apple Cider Vinegar — Discussed in the video primarily in relation to blood-sugar and metabolic health rather than as a direct treatment for neuropathy.
Alpha-Lipoic Acid (ALA) — An antioxidant that has been studied particularly for symptoms associated with diabetic peripheral neuropathy.
Magnesium — Important for normal nerve and muscle function and involved in hundreds of biochemical reactions throughout the body.

Michael Kim returns as defending champion to play in Europe for the first time since July, but this time he’ll be playing at a completely different course. videos.title: Google's Gemini Notebook Is Becoming an AI Research Workspace
videos.summary_source_text:
Google's Gemini Notebook Is Becoming an AI Research Workspace https://bitbiased.ai/ai-automation-services

Google renamed NotebookLM to Gemini Notebook — but the rebrand is the least interesting part. The bigger change is that every notebook can now come with what Google calls a “secure cloud computer,” allowing Gemini to write and execute Python code against your own documents instead of simply summarizing them.

That pushes Gemini Notebook much closer to a full research platform. It can answer questions from source material with clickable citations, generate podcast-style Audio Overviews, create narrated slide videos, build quizzes and flashcards, analyze data with Python, and even pull eligible Google Play ebooks you own directly into a notebook.

But there are some important catches.

Gemini Notebook is still source-grounded, not automatically fact-checked. A citation proves where an answer came from — it doesn’t prove the answer is correct. Conflicting sources can still cause problems, scanned PDFs and poor transcripts can contaminate everything built from them, and Google itself says users should verify generated answers against the original material.

The new cloud computer is arguably the biggest technical leap. Gemini can extract information from documents, write Python, execute calculations, and return tables or charts. That puts it in territory already familiar to users of ChatGPT’s Code Interpreter. However, the feature initially arrived for Google AI Ultra and Workspace Ultra users, only Python executes automatically, and questions remain around exactly how persistent these compute environments are.

Then there’s the multimedia side. Audio Overviews turn research into AI-hosted podcast conversations, while interactive voice lets you interrupt and ask questions. Video Overviews create narrated slide presentations, and Short Video Overviews compress individual ideas into roughly 60-second vertical explainers. These aren’t AI-generated movies — they’re closer to automatically assembled presentations.

Gemini Notebook is also becoming a serious study tool, with flashcards, quizzes, mind maps, study guides, and Google’s LearnLM technology sitting behind parts of the education experience.

And Google is expanding what counts as a “source.” Expert Intelligence lets users import eligible Google Play ebooks they already own, with Google saying more than 100,000 titles were supported at launch. Instead of relying on what an AI model remembers about a book, Gemini Notebook can work directly from the purchased text.

That matters because this increasingly looks like an ecosystem play. Notebook content already connects with Gemini, while Google has said integration with Search’s AI Mode is coming. Combine that with Gemini appearing across Gmail and Docs, and your notebooks could become a persistent context layer across more of Google’s products.

Google says Gemini Notebook has passed 30 million users and 600,000 organizations, but the practical limitations still matter. Usage is constrained by compute quotas, demanding features like audio and video consume that budget faster, and free notebooks have source limits. Paid plans range from AI Plus and AI Pro through AI Ultra, with higher tiers getting larger quotas and earlier access to advanced features.

So what actually changed when NotebookLM became Gemini Notebook? We break down the cloud computer, source grounding, Audio and Video Overviews, Expert Intelligence, pricing and limits, Google’s wider ecosystem strategy, and where Gemini Notebook still falls short compared with tools like ChatGPT and Claude.

videos.title: If You Never Learned This, You Were Taught To Protect The Puck The Slow Way
videos.summary_source_text:
If You Never Learned This, You Were Taught To Protect The Puck The Slow Way The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

In a clinical trial involving 120 healthy people, participants were given omeprazole. None had heartburn or acid reflux at the start of the trial, yet afterward, nearly half developed heartburn, indigestion, or acid reflux.

Acid reflux isn’t always a problem of too much stomach acid. In fact, many people with GERD and acid reflux may actually have low stomach acid.

Antacids aren’t meant to be taken long term; however, many people use them for extended periods. Side effects associated with long-term use can include nutritional deficiencies, anxiety, depression, and more.

Overeating, a hiatal hernia, and high-sugar diets can also contribute to heartburn and acid reflux.

Betaine hydrochloride can help acidify the stomach and may help reduce GERD symptoms. Zinc carnosine can also support digestive health if you’re dealing with an ulcer or stomach inflammation.

videos.summary_source_text:
Stop Doing C-Cuts Skate Like This Instead The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

Do These 6 Things | Dr. Mandell If stubborn belly fat just doesn’t seem to go away despite your best efforts, there may be more to consider than simply doing more crunches or adding more cardio. In this video, Dr. Alan Mandell explains six important lifestyle and nutrition changes that can help create a healthier environment for your body to access stored fat. You’ll learn why giving your body adequate time between meals can allow insulin levels to come down, how starting meals with protein and soluble fiber can slow digestion and help control blood sugar and appetite, and why foods such as oats, chia seeds, flax seeds, psyllium, lentils, beans, and certain fruits can benefit both metabolic health and your gut microbiome. We’ll also discuss why frequently drinking sugary carbohydrates can work against your goals, how quality sleep influences insulin sensitivity and stress hormones, and why managing chronic stress is an important part of the picture. These six changes aren’t about starving yourself or spending endless hours exercising—they’re about understanding how your body responds to food, sleep, stress, and daily habits and then using that knowledge to make better choices consistently. videos.title: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Is a Freak: 552B Parameters, Only 8B Active
videos.summary_source_text:
DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Is a Freak: 552B Parameters, Only 8B Active https://bitbiased.ai/ai-automation-services

DeepSeek says V4.1-Flash scored 90.6 on Terminal-Bench 2.1, ahead of Claude Opus 5 at 89.1 and GPT-5.6 Sol at 88.8. Even more striking: this is a 552-billion-parameter model that activates just 8 billion parameters per input token.

But that headline needs context.

DeepSeek V4.1-Flash arrived on September 10 with open weights under an MIT license, native vision, a one-million-token context window, and an architecture designed around a simple reality of AI agents: they spend far more tokens reading than writing. DeepSeek's answer is to make that reading dramatically cheaper.

One real-world test shows why this matters. DataCamp gave V4.1-Flash a screenshot of a broken Flask dashboard and access to the underlying project. Without being told where the bugs were, the agent identified problems across Python, CSS, and JavaScript and produced a three-file patch. All five tests passed.

Then there was a problem: the webpage was still wrong.

The agent correctly diagnosed that the Flask server was running stale code, but it had no tool to restart it before hitting its turn limit. A human restart was required. It's a useful example of the difference between fixing code and actually completing an autonomous software task.

The entire run involved 156,724 input tokens, with an 87% cache hit rate, plus 11,497 output tokens. Reported off-peak cost: about one cent.

That efficiency comes from some unusual architecture. V4.1-Flash combines mixture-of-experts routing with a split encoder-decoder design. DeepSeek says only 8 billion parameters are active per token during input processing and 16 billion during generation. Its KV cache is also just 890 bytes per token, using compressed sparse attention, 4-bit cache storage, and on-demand reconstruction.

At DeepSeek's off-peak pricing, cached input costs $0.003 per million tokens. That sounds almost absurdly cheap—but price per token isn't necessarily price per completed task.

So we go through DeepSeek's benchmark table line by line.

V4.1-Flash scores 90.6 on Terminal-Bench 2.1, 74.2 on DeepSWE, 88.1 on CyberGym, and 54.8 on AutomationBench. But harder benchmarks tell a different story. On Terminal-Bench 3.0 it scores 30.0 versus 43.3 for Claude Opus 5, while Terminal-Bench 4.0 shows 31.2 versus 51.8. DeepSeek's own results also show that changing the agent harness can move its DeepSWE score from 65.5 to 74.2.

Then there's the competition DeepSeek's original chart didn't include. Around the same period, newer models arrived from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and xAI, including GPT-6 Luna, GPT-6 Sol, Claude Opus 5.5, Gemini 3.8 Flash, and Grok 4.7. That changes how V4.1-Flash's headline comparisons should be interpreted.

Independent Artificial Analysis testing adds another piece: V4.1-Flash scored 39 on its Intelligence Index versus 36 for V4-Pro and reached roughly 227 tokens per second. But it also generated substantially more output tokens than the median comparable model, pushing its measured cost per task to $0.27.

So is DeepSeek V4.1-Flash actually a frontier-model killer, or is its real achievement something more interesting: making long-context, input-heavy AI agents dramatically cheaper to run?

We break down the architecture, pricing, benchmarks, independent testing, limitations, and what DeepSeek's upcoming V4.1-Pro could mean next. :contentReference[oaicite:0]{index=0}

videos.title: “Fable 5.2” Just DESTROYED GPT-6 Astra
videos.summary_source_text:
“Fable 5.2” Just DESTROYED GPT-6 Astra https://bitbiased.ai/ai-automation-services

A supposed “Fable 5.2” is being credited with beating GPT-6 Astra, quietly appearing inside Claude Code, and delivering major coding and visual-generation upgrades. But there’s one problem: Anthropic has never announced a model called Fable 5.2.

As of September 21st, Anthropic’s official page still lists Claude Fable 5.1 as its most capable model for ambitious coding projects. There’s no Fable 5.2 model ID, pricing page, system card, benchmark table, or launch announcement.

So where did the rumor come from — and is there actually a secret Anthropic model being tested?

The trail starts on September 1st, when investor Gavin Baker speculated that Anthropic might already have “Fable 5.2” ready. After OpenAI released GPT-6 Astra on September 3rd, that speculation accelerated. Within days, social-media posts were claiming Anthropic’s next Fable could come from an entirely new pretraining run and arrive by late September or early October.

Then users began claiming they were actually encountering the mystery model inside Claude Code.

Some testers reported that Fable 5.1 sessions appeared to be routing to a “next Fable” model. One unusual test involved asking Claude about “Tibo the reset guy,” with users treating knowledge of that recent niche reference as evidence that they had reached a newer checkpoint.

But that test has a major problem: getting the answer right doesn’t reveal which model produced it. Different post-training data, hidden context, memory, retrieval, A/B testing, effort settings, or another checkpoint could potentially produce the same result.

Anthropic does officially document model routing in certain circumstances, so the underlying infrastructure exists. What hasn’t surfaced is an API model identifier, network artifact, billing identifier, leaked system card, or other technical evidence proving regular users are secretly being routed to “Fable 5.2.”

The viral demos have similar limitations. One Reddit user reported that a suspected newer model made real progress on coding projects where Fable 5.1 had struggled, including choosing a state-machine architecture for a Rust networking protocol. A September 19th visual comparison also appeared to show the mystery model going head-to-head with GPT-6 Astra.

Interesting evidence — but neither confirms the backend model.

There’s another complication: Fable 5.1 is already extremely capable. Anthropic says it has a 1-million-token context window, up to 128,000 output tokens, adaptive thinking, and substantial improvements across coding, terminal, browser-agent, and knowledge-work tasks. Different effort settings alone can also produce noticeable changes in quality, speed, and cost.

That means an impressive coding result, frontend demo, game, SVG, or 3D generation isn't automatically evidence of a secret model.

Then Reuters added the strongest evidence yet. On September 19th, Reuters reported, citing three sources, that Anthropic was considering rolling out a new AI model, with one source saying it was undergoing safety evaluation.

That matters — but Reuters did NOT call it Fable 5.2, did not report that it came from a new pretraining run, and did not provide a release date.

So this investigation separates what we can actually substantiate from what the internet has gradually converted into “fact”: the origins of the Fable 5.2 name, the alleged new pretraining run, Claude Code routing reports, the viral Astra comparisons, what Fable 5.1 can already do, the Reuters report, and the alternative explanations that could account for the mystery-model sightings.

Something new may genuinely be under evaluation at Anthropic. The much bigger question is what that model actually is.

What hasn’t surfaced is an API model identifier, network artifact, billing identifier, leaked system card, or other technical evidence proving regular users are secretly being routed to “Fable 5.2.”

The viral demos have similar limitations. One Reddit user reported that a suspected newer model made real progress on coding projects where Fable 5.1 had struggled, including choosing a state-machine architecture for a Rust networking protocol. A September 19th visual comparison also appeared to show the mystery model going head-to-head with GPT-6 Astra.

Interesting evidence — but neither confirms the backend model.

There’s another complication: Fable 5.1 is already extremely capable. Anthropic says it has a 1-million-token context window, up to 128,000 output tokens, adaptive thinking, and substantial improvements across coding, terminal, browser-agent, and knowledge-work tasks. Different effort settings alone can also produce noticeable changes in quality, speed, and cost.

That means an impressive coding result, frontend demo, game, SVG, or 3D generation isn't automatically evidence of a secret model.

Then Reuters added the strongest evidence yet. On September 19th, Reuters reported, citing three sources, that Anthropic was considering rolling out a new AI model, with one source saying it was undergoing safety evaluation.

That matters — but Reuters did NOT call it Fable 5.2, did not report that it came from a new pretraining run, and did not provide a release date.

So this investigation separates what we can actually substantiate from what the internet has gradually converted into “fact”: the origins of the Fable 5.2 name, the alleged new pretraining run, Claude Code routing reports, the viral Astra comparisons, what Fable 5.1 can already do, the Reuters report, and the alternative explanations that could account for the mystery-model sightings.

Something new may genuinely be under evaluation at Anthropic. The much bigger question is what that model actually is.

A Confident Saucer Breaks Systems Faster Than Any Deke The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

videos.summary_source_text: This Mobility Test Explains Your Swing  #golfswing #golftips This simple 90/90 mobility test gives you a clear look at how your right arm should function in the golf swing. From a 5-iron posture, lift and rotate the arm until it matches your spine angle—if you can’t get there, your backswing is likely compensating by standing up or losing posture. That compensation often leads to poor ball striking and inconsistent contact. Your swing should reflect what your body can actually do, even if that means a shorter backswing. videos.title: Before Hitting Your Woods - Make This 5 Second Change
videos.summary_source_text:
Before Hitting Your Woods - Make This 5 Second Change Fairway woods and hybrids should make golf easier… but for a lot of golfers they’re some of the hardest clubs in the bag to hit consistently.

Tops, thin shots, heavy strikes and weak shots to the right can quickly destroy your confidence.

And according to Shot Scope, the average golfer uses a fairway wood or hybrid for around 25% of their shots — so learning how to strike them properly can make a huge difference to your scores.

In this golf lesson, Danny Maude shows you two simple drills to help you hit your fairway woods and hybrids cleaner, straighter and with more distance.

The first drill helps you improve your ball striking and understand how the club should travel through impact.

The second helps you create more speed and naturally square the clubface — without trying to manipulate your golf swing.

If you struggle to hit fairway woods off the ground, top your 3 wood, thin your hybrids or slice them to the right, this lesson should really help.

You’ll discover:

• Why golfers top fairway woods and hybrids  
• Why thin shots can happen for a completely different reason  
• The ideal strike for a fairway wood off the ground  
• A simple finish position that can improve your contact  
• Why the trail shoulder matters through impact  
• How to create a shallow, sweeping strike with fairway woods  
• The ball position I recommend for a fairway wood  
• A simple drill you can use before you play  
• Why forcing positions can make your swing feel wooden  
• How opening the clubface can actually help a golfer who slices  
• How to square the clubface naturally through impact  
• Why releasing the club can create more speed and distance  
• How to hit fairway woods with a powerful sweeping motion  
• How to know whether you are too steep or leaning back in your golf swing  

One of the biggest mistakes golfers make with fairway woods is trying to lift the golf ball into the air.

The club already has loft.

Your job is to create a strike where the club travels beautifully through the ball and brushes the turf — allowing the loft of the club to launch the golf ball for you.

Once you understand that sensation, fairway woods and hybrids can start to feel dramatically easier.

#golfswing #golftips #golfinstruction Fairway woods and hybrids should make golf easier… but for a lot of golfers they’re some of the hardest clubs in the bag to hit consistently.

Tops, thin shots, heavy strikes and weak shots to the right can quickly destroy your confidence.

And according to Shot Scope, the average golfer uses a fairway wood or hybrid for around 25% of their shots — so learning how to strike them properly can make a huge difference to your scores.

In this golf lesson, Danny Maude shows you two simple drills to help you hit your fairway woods and hybrids cleaner, straighter and with more distance.

The first drill helps you improve your ball striking and understand how the club should travel through impact.

The second helps you create more speed and naturally square the clubface — without trying to manipulate your golf swing.

If you struggle to hit fairway woods off the ground, top your 3 wood, thin your hybrids or slice them to the right, this lesson should really help.

• Why golfers top fairway woods and hybrids

• Why releasing the club can create more speed and distance  
• How to hit fairway woods with a powerful sweeping motion  
• How to know whether you are too steep or leaning back in your golf swing  

One of the biggest mistakes golfers make with fairway woods is trying to lift the golf ball into the air.

The club already has loft.

Your job is to create a strike where the club travels beautifully through the ball and brushes the turf — allowing the loft of the club to launch the golf ball for you.

Once you understand that sensation, fairway woods and hybrids can start to feel dramatically easier.

Then we come to the all-new RS5. As with the second generation, it comes with a 2.9-litre twin-turbo V6. However, this is accompanied by an electric motor, and they combine to create 639hp and 825Nm! Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

RIFT — THE NEXT-GEN AFFILIATE OS

No More Toe Drags The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

Here are 7 common symptoms of hypothyroidism you may not have realized are related to your thyroid:

1. Eyebrow changes
Disappearing outer thirds of your eyebrows? Thyroid hormones power your hair follicles, so hair loss in this area can signal a thyroid issue.

2. High cholesterol levels
High cholesterol often leads to immediate medication prescriptions. But did you know a slow thyroid can cause this imbalance? Addressing it may normalize your cholesterol levels.

3. Puffy face
Waking up with facial puffiness? This could indicate your thyroid is trapping water beneath the skin, a common symptom of thyroid dysfunction.

4. Carpal tunnel syndrome
Fluid accumulation around the median nerve can be a result of hypothyroidism, and swelling can lead to carpal tunnel syndrome.

5. Mood changes
Feeling depressed or anxious? Over 50% of those with a slow thyroid experience mood disorders. Thyroid hormones are essential for energy production in your brain.

6. Persistent headaches
Thyroid issues can cause muscle tightness in your neck. This tension may lead to headaches or migraines due to locked-up muscles.

7. Low body temperature
Use a thermometer to monitor your morning temperature. If it’s below 97.8°F, consider a slow thyroid as a possible cause.

3. Puffy face
Waking up with facial puffiness? This could indicate your thyroid is trapping water beneath the skin, a common symptom of thyroid dysfunction.

4. Carpal tunnel syndrome
Fluid accumulation around the median nerve can be a result of hypothyroidism, and swelling can lead to carpal tunnel syndrome.

5. Mood changes
Feeling depressed or anxious? Over 50% of those with a slow thyroid experience mood disorders. Thyroid hormones are essential for energy production in your brain.

6. Persistent headaches
Thyroid issues can cause muscle tightness in your neck. This tension may lead to headaches or migraines due to locked-up muscles.

7. Low body temperature
Use a thermometer to monitor your morning temperature. If it’s below 97.8°F, consider a slow thyroid as a possible cause.

ELECTRIC FACTORY IN GREENSBORO! Carolina Hurricanes' Mike Maniscalco Joins to Talk Greensboro & HHN The Carolina Hurricanes returned to Greensboro on Thursday night and brought fans a show. They erased a four-goal deficit and won 6-5 in the dying seconds. Mike Maniscalco joins to talk about it all and more. On the Friday Edition of Locked On Hurricanes, Zach and Mike kick off the show by discussing the electric atmosphere of Thursday night's preseason game in Greensboro. After being gone for 25 years, the first game back had everything and more. How did both guys feel about the growth of hockey and how the night encapsulated what the Hurricanes have done to build the game in NC? Secondly, the guys discuss what fans can expect from the new Hurricanes Hockey Network this upcoming season. How awesome is it that the Hurricanes brought everyone back as the best TV crew in hockey? Lastly, Zach and Mike talk about Bussi, Kochetkov, and the upcoming 2026-27 season. How much fun will it be seeing the Hurricanes defend a title instead of chasing one? All of that and more, on the latest edition of Locked On Hurricanes.
