videos.title: Hindi - 22.09.26 - Rift Presentation
videos.summary_source_text:
Hindi - 22.09.26 - Rift Presentation RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

videos.summary_source_text:
This Is The Skill Nobody Trains And Everyone Wonders Why They Lose The Puck The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

videos.summary_source_text:
Bästa fonderna för pensionen? Marie har 18 år kvar till pension och undrar vilken fond hon ska välja.

Svaret är samma som i våras, samma som förra året, och samma som för tio år sedan. Ingenting har förändrats.

Forskningen är ganska entydig om vad som har bäst odds framgent:

- Bred
- Billig
- Global
- Passiv indexfond

Alltså: äg hela höstacken i stället för att leta nålarna. Då får du med nålarna på vägen.

Helt konkret: gå till din bank eller din valcentral och leta efter en fond som har global i namnet, har index i namnet och kostar under 0,2 procent. Hittar du ingen finns vår lista per bank på rikatillsammans.se under Spara och investera, Bästa fonderna.

Och eftersom vi pratar konkret fond: historisk avkastning är ingen garanti för framtida avkastning. Du kan förlora delar av eller hela ditt kapital. Läs riskinformationen.

videos.title: Gemini 4 Pro Just Leaked: The Results Are Insane
videos.summary_source_text:
Gemini 4 Pro Just Leaked: The Results Are Insane https://bitbiased.ai/ai-automation-services

A mysterious Gemini model started producing surprisingly advanced interactive games and SVG demos inside Arena — while being labeled as the already-released Gemini 3.8 Flash. Just days earlier, an X account claimed to have leaked Gemini 4 Pro under the internal codename “Argon,” with a massive 2-million-token context window and 256,000-token output limit.

So did Google quietly put Gemini 4 Pro into Arena for public testing, or is the internet connecting dots that were never connected?

The mystery started with unusually capable Arena outputs: an interactive pelican riding a bicycle, a teapot with working controls, and eventually a playable Ultraman-versus-Godzilla browser game complete with animations, enemies, lasers, and a functioning score counter. Every one of these outputs appeared under the Gemini 3.8 Flash name.

That immediately fueled speculation that Google was disguising an unreleased Gemini 4 checkpoint.

And the timing made the theory even more compelling. Three days before the Arena sightings, the X account Lentils80 posted what it claimed was the first leaked output from Gemini 4 Pro “Argon.” The alleged model reportedly had a 2-million-token context window and 256K output ceiling — dramatically beyond the documented Gemini 3.8 Flash limits.

But there’s a major problem: none of those Argon specifications have been independently verified.

Google has confirmed that Gemini 4 exists only in a much narrower sense. Sundar Pichai said in July that Google DeepMind had begun its “most ambitious pre-training run yet for Gemini 4.” Google did not confirm a Gemini 4 Pro model, the Argon codename, those leaked specifications, or a release date.

There’s also precedent for fake Gemini 4 leaks. An August “Gemini 4 Pro benchmark” supposedly showed extraordinary scores, including 99.9% on ARC-AGI-3. Those numbers were later found to match published results attributed to a competing OpenAI model, suggesting the supposed Gemini benchmark had simply been relabeled.

Then comes potentially the biggest problem for the Argon theory.

At least one Arena tester reportedly reproduced the mysterious output quality by selecting “gemini-3.8-flash-high” — a higher-thinking configuration of the existing Gemini 3.8 Flash model. There’s also a significant speed mismatch: the alleged Argon generation reportedly took 2.4 minutes, while some supposed Gemini 4 comparisons took far longer. The mysterious Arena demos could return in seconds.

There’s no “Argon” fingerprint hidden in the generated code, no leaked model card, no API listing, and no Gemini 4 entry on Arena’s scored leaderboard.

Still, the creative coding performance is difficult to ignore. The model produced polished, interactive experiences that surprised testers and generated comparisons with other frontier models. Something about these outputs caught the community’s attention — the unresolved question is whether that “something” is a secret Gemini 4 checkpoint, a higher-reasoning Gemini 3.8 Flash configuration, narrow optimization, or something else entirely.

We break down the Arena sightings, the Argon leak, the evidence for and against the Gemini 4 theory, the previously debunked benchmark leak, and exactly what Google has — and hasn’t — officially confirmed.

CHAPTERS

02:02 The Arena Sightings
04:05 The Argon Leak
06:03 Is This Actually A New Model?
08:42 The Case For And The Case Against
11:19 What We Still Don't Know

videos.title: Grok 4.7 Just Dropped… This Is a BIG Upgrade
videos.summary_source_text:
Grok 4.7 Just Dropped… This Is a BIG Upgrade https://bitbiased.ai/ai-automation-services

Grok 4.7 just jumped from 31.9% to 46.0% on SWE-Marathon — a 44% relative improvement in just six weeks. But when independent lab Artificial Analysis tested xAI’s new model, its composite score moved from 44 to just 46… while generating more than twice as many output tokens.

That gap between xAI’s headline benchmarks and independent testing is where Grok 4.7 gets interesting.

xAI announced Grok 4.7 on September 21, 2026, just 40 days after Grok 4.6. According to xAI, this is a new, larger base model with longer supplemental training, curated reasoning data, advanced technical corpora, an improved training recipe, and heavier reinforcement learning on difficult multi-hour agentic tasks.

But most regular Grok users can’t actually use it yet. Grok 4.7 launched through the xAI API, Grok Build, Cursor, and Microsoft Office add-ins first, while access through Grok’s web and mobile apps and Grok on X is coming later.

The headline improvements are concentrated around coding and long-running agents. We break down DeepSWE, Terminal-Bench 4.0, FrontierSWE V2, SWE-Marathon, and CursorBench 4.0 individually — including where Grok 4.7 makes clean gains and where reasoning-effort differences make xAI’s comparisons less straightforward.

There are some impressive numbers. Grok 4.7 reaches 71.0% on DeepSWE and jumps to 46.0% on SWE-Marathon. But competitors including GPT-5.6 Sol, Claude Fable 5.1, and Opus 5 still lead several of these coding benchmarks.

The bigger story may be agents that can work for hours. xAI tested Grok 4.7 on software engineering tasks with time budgets reaching 20 hours and is increasingly positioning Grok for professional work beyond coding: legal documents, spreadsheets, presentations, CAD, electrical engineering, biological data, and other complex workflows.

Then comes the independent reality check.

Artificial Analysis scored Grok 4.7 high at 46 on its Intelligence Index, compared with 44 for Grok 4.6 high. But its evaluation produced roughly 200 million output tokens for 4.7 versus about 94 million for 4.6. Measured cost per evaluated task also increased from $1.86 to $2.73. Same list price per token does not necessarily mean the same cost per completed task.

Pricing itself remains $2 per million input tokens and $6 per million output tokens for standard requests at or below 200,000 tokens. Go beyond that threshold and the entire request moves to the higher long-context pricing tier. We compare that with GPT-6 Astra, GPT-5.6 Sol, Claude Fable 5.1, and Gemini 3.8 Flash — and look at whether Grok can still claim a meaningful price advantage.

We also dig into xAI’s safety card. Several jailbreak and harmful-compliance measurements improved, while general harmful-request compliance and the self-harm metric moved slightly in the wrong direction. Some biosecurity-related capability scores also declined intentionally, according to xAI, as part of its safety training approach.

And there are still major unanswered questions: no parameter count, no disclosed dense-vs-MoE architecture, no training compute or cost, no standalone long-context benchmark, and no general computer-use tool.

Grok 4.7 is clearly more than a rename. The question is whether its gains justify how much more inference it may need to produce them.

CHAPTERS

00:00 Grok 4.7’s Huge Benchmark Jump Has a Catch
01:12 What Actually Shipped, and Where You Can't Use It Yet
02:42 What xAI Actually Changed Under the Hood
04:22 The Coding Benchmarks, One at a Time
06:58 Agents That Work for Hours, and the Push Into Professional Work
09:06 The Independent Reality Check
11:09 The Price Tag, and the Fine Print xAI Didn't Put in the Headline
13:00 What Got Safer, and What Quietly Got Worse
14:30 What xAI Still Won't Tell You

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

What are the four fundamentals that matter most for becoming a better golfer? In this video, we break down the key positions and movements that can have the biggest impact on your ball striking: setup, club path, clubface, and keeping the club in front of you throughout the swing.

You’ll learn why club path is one of the most common problems golfers struggle with, how an outside-in or overly inside path can lead to slices, hooks, shanks, fat shots, and tops, and how simple alignment-stick drills can help you improve your path. We also look at the importance of a square clubface, including how small changes in clubface position during the backswing can dramatically affect ball flight.

Finally, we get into the foundation of the entire swing: your setup. Proper distance from the ball, alignment, ball position, and grip all influence your ability to swing the club correctly. The fourth fundamental—keeping the club in front of you—can also help improve both your path and clubface. If you're trying to hit the ball more consistently and understand the root causes of your swing mistakes, these four fundamentals are a great place to start.

videos.title: INSIDE PATH—STILL SLICING?
videos.summary_source_text:
INSIDE PATH—STILL SLICING? You can swing from the inside and still hit a huge slice.

Why? Because fixing your club path is only half the equation. If the clubface stays open relative to that path, the ball can start right and curve even farther right.

The goal isn’t just to swing from the inside, it’s to match your clubface to your path through impact.
That’s where the Blue Brick can help. It gives you a clear visual reference for your swing direction, helping you build an inside path you can repeat while learning to deliver the club more consistently. Instead of guessing what your club is doing, you can see it and train it.

Fix the path. Match the face. Start hitting straighter, more powerful shots!

Check the link in the comments!
